resources.string: Ask the first provider. If it fails or has no results, ask the next one.
Ask all providers at the same time and mix their results in one grid.
Each provider gets its own chip. Tap a chip to see its results.
The panel shows the providers that are on. Choose one there, and only that one is asked.
Providers of the same kind act as one. The first is asked, and the next only when it fails, for example when a key runs out of quota.
Each one is its own provider: its own chip, its own choice in the panel, its own share of a mixed grid.
No provider is on. Turn one on in this tool\'s settings.
GIFs and stickers. Needs a KLIPY API key, unless this build has one.
GIFs and stickers. Always in its own tab: GIPHY does not let apps mix its results with others.
Free GIFs and photos from Wikimedia Commons, or from your own MediaWiki. No key. The GIFs are mostly educational.
Old GeoCities GIFs from the Internet Archive. No key. The results have no content rating.
GIF packs that you imported. They work with no connection.
Your sticker packs on this phone.
Translates on the phone with Google\'s ML Kit. Your text stays on the phone. Each language needs a model download first.

Translates on the phone with Mozilla\'s Bergamot engine and the Firefox Translations models. Free software, no Google services, and your text stays on the phone. Each direction (French to English, English to French) is its own download of 14 to 37 MB. Needs a 64-bit phone with Android 9 or later.

Translates on the phone with Meta\'s NLLB-200 model on CTranslate2: 200 languages, between any two of them, for the pairs the other engines cannot do. One download of 630 MB, and a sentence takes a few seconds. Your text stays on the phone. The model is licensed for non-commercial use only (CC BY-NC 4.0). Needs a 64-bit phone with 6 GB of memory or more.
A server that answers OpenAI chat requests: llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or a gateway.
Needs your DeepL API key, or the address of a proxy that adds one.
A LibreTranslate server: your own or a public one. Public servers usually need a key.
A Mozhi server: a free front end to Google, DeepL, DuckDuckGo, Yandex and Reverso. Choose the engine. DeepL and Reverso need a source language.
A SimplyTranslate server: a free front end to Google and other engines.
A Lingva server: a free front end to Google Translate.
A Translite server: a free front end to Google Translate.
A Rens server: a free front end to Google Lens. It reads the text in a photo for you, in most scripts.
A Rens server: a free front end to Google Lens. It gives the photo back with its text translated.
A model that reads images, through a server that answers OpenAI chat requests. Needs the address and the model name.
Google\'s free endpoint, or Cloud Translation when you add a key.
A SearXNG instance that allows JSON results. Most public instances do not.
Web search with a short answer. Needs your Tavily key.
Web and image search. Needs a Brave Search API key, unless this build has one.
Photos from Unsplash. Needs an API key, unless this build has one.
Photos from Pexels. Needs an API key, unless this build has one.
Daily rates for most currencies. No key.
European Central Bank rates for the main currencies. Free software, no key.
European Central Bank reference rates, plus official rates from 120 central banks. No key.
Currencies and coins from Coinbase. No key.
Open data for most currencies and many coins. No key.
Coin prices from CoinGecko. No key.
Your own Home Assistant server. Every kind of thing, live, with Assist.
The devices in your Google Home, through Play services. One home at a time; you choose which in Google\'s own screen.
Your SmartThings devices, rooms and scenes, through Samsung\'s cloud. States refresh while the panel is open.
Lights, rooms, scenes and sensors straight from a Hue bridge on your Wi-Fi. Nothing leaves the house.
An openHAB server: its items, live, with rooms from the semantic model.
Smart Life and Tuya Smart devices, rooms and scenes, through a free Tuya developer project linked to your app account. States refresh while the panel is open.
Your SwitchBot devices, infrared remotes and scenes, through SwitchBot\'s cloud with the token from its app. States refresh once a minute while the panel is open.
Claude models through Anthropic\'s API, with your own key.
GPT models through OpenAI\'s API, with your own key.
Gemini models through Google\'s API, with your own key from AI Studio.
Grok models through xAI\'s API, with your own key.
DeepSeek models through DeepSeek\'s API, with your own key.
Answers grounded in a Brave web search. Needs a key with the Answers plan. Left blank, the Brave Search key you typed for web search is tried.
Models on an Ollama server you run, on your computer or your network. Add one for each server.
Models served by LM Studio on your computer. Add one for each computer.
Any other service with OpenAI\'s chat API: OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, Together, or a gateway of your own. Give the address up to the version, such as https://openrouter.ai/api/v1.
A model downloaded to this phone. Nothing you write leaves it. Pick and download the model on the AI page.
The speech recognizer that comes with the phone, usually Google\'s. Words appear as you speak.
A small, fast model that runs on the phone. Download it on the Voice typing page.
OpenAI\'s Whisper models, run on the phone. Many languages; download a model on the Voice typing page.
English dictation on the phone, with words appearing as you speak.
A large model that runs on the phone and understands 25 European languages.
A tiny, quick English model that runs on the phone.
Streaming models for 13 languages, Bangla among them, that type as you speak, on the phone.
Meta\'s one model for 1,600 languages, hundreds of them with no other voice typing, on the phone. Each phrase arrives at the pause after it.
A server that speaks OpenAI\'s audio transcription API: speaches, whisper.cpp\'s server, LocalAI, Groq or OpenAI. Each clip is sent to it when you stop speaking.
The grammar engine built into the keyboard. English only, and nothing you type leaves the phone.
Grammar, spelling and style in more than 30 languages. Your text is sent to a LanguageTool server to be checked: the public one at api.languagetool.org unless you enter your own.
A model downloaded to this phone, or one you imported. Nothing you type leaves it. Pick the model on the generator\'s screen.
Free, with no key and no account: the prompt is sent to Pollinations, which picks the model. A key from enter.pollinations.ai opens its newer API and lets you name a model.
Free Stable Diffusion on volunteers\' computers. Works without a key but waits in a queue; a free key from aihorde.net moves you up it.
GPT Image, which draws stickers on a transparent background. Paid per picture. A blank key uses the OpenAI key from the AI tool.
Google\'s Nano Banana image models. A blank key uses the Gemini key from the AI tool.
xAI\'s image model. A blank key uses the xAI key from the AI tool.
Stable Image Core, Ultra and Stable Diffusion 3.5 from the makers of Stable Diffusion. Paid in credits; needs a key from platform.stability.ai.
The FLUX models from the people who made them. Needs a key from bfl.ai.
Illustrations, icons and vector-style art. Needs a key from recraft.ai.
Thousands of hosted models. Name any text-to-image model as owner/name; FLUX Schnell when blank.
Fast hosted models: FLUX, Recraft, Ideogram, Qwen Image and more. Name the model\'s fal id; FLUX Schnell when blank.
FLUX and other open models on Together\'s servers.
Models on Hugging Face\'s own inference servers, with a free monthly allowance. Needs an access token with Inference Providers permission.
FLUX and Stable Diffusion on Cloudflare, with a free daily allowance. Needs an API token and your account id.
Your own Stable Diffusion web UI, started with --api. Give its address, such as http://192.168.1.10:7860.
Your own ComfyUI server. Draws with a plain text-to-image workflow and the checkpoint you name, or the first one it has.
Any other service with OpenAI\'s image API: LocalAI, DeepInfra, Nebius, or a gateway of your own. Give the address up to the version, such as https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai.
Recognises most released music from a few seconds of sound. Needs a token from dashboard.audd.io; a few hundred recognitions are free, then it is paid. Each clip is sent to AudD.
A music recognition service with a two-week trial, then paid plans. Needs the host, access key and access secret of a project from console.acrcloud.com. Each clip is sent to ACRCloud.
A small recognition service, free for personal use with a key from audiotag.info, and slower than the others: it answers after a few seconds. Each clip is sent to AudioTag.
Shazam\'s catalogue through an unofficial listing on RapidAPI, with a RapidAPI key. Not an Apple service: the listing may change or stop without notice. Each clip is sent to RapidAPI.
A server you run that answers like AudD: the clip is posted as a file and the song comes back as JSON. Put a fingerprinter such as Panako or Olaf behind it.
Cloudflare\'s speed test servers, the nearest of its data centres. Needs no account, and tells the card which network you are on and which city answered.
A LibreSpeed server: one you run yourself, or one of the volunteers\' servers from the public list, picked by city on the row\'s own screen.
